description: Where the real chokepoint is: not the mines, but the refineries
verification_status: confirmed (IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026, Cobalt Institute/Statista, multiple analytical sources)
key_thesis: The original source documents measure China's influence by its share of extraction (~80% of DRC cobalt). But the real lever is midstream: China controls 70-80% of world cobalt refining, while the DRC refines less than 5% of its own output. Even minerals shipped via the 'Western' Lobito corridor mostly come from Chinese-capitalized mines and still end up at Chinese refineries.

value_chain.share: 70-76% of world cobalt output; ~3.4 million tonnes of copper in 2025 (~15% of world output)
value_chain.china_control: ~72-80% of DRC's copper-cobalt assets; per the Atlantic Council, a stake in 15 of 19 cobalt mines

value_chain.share: 70-80% of world cobalt refining capacity (estimates vary: 70%, 75%, 77%, 80% across sources); ~73% of lithium; ~65% of nickel
value_chain.drc_control: less than 5% of its own output is refined domestically

value_chain.share: dominant in precursors, cathodes, and cell manufacturing
value_chain.note: in October 2025 China imposed export controls on cathode materials, precursors, and graphite anodes - the same weapon the DRC now applies to raw materials

china_financing.coverage: official Chinese loans and grants for extraction/processing of 32 critical minerals across 47 countries
china_financing.structure: 92% of financing goes to extraction, only 8% to local processing; 83% of loans go to mines fully or partly owned by Chinese companies
china_financing.source: AidData, Chinese Financing for Transition Minerals Dataset v2.0
china_financing.implication: institutionally locks the DRC into the role of raw-material supplier

why_it_matters: The DRC's ban on exporting concentrates (June 2026) is the first attempt by Kinshasa to attack midstream directly, rather than simply trading in volumes. But without solving the power-supply shortfall (estimated at ~3,000 MW by the minister), building domestic smelting capacity is impossible - which loops back to the hydropower cascade, controlled by the same Chinese companies.
